items.headline: OpenAI releases GPT-6 Cyber to vetted security customers
items.summary: OpenAI launched a cybersecurity-focused variant of GPT-6 for authorized vulnerability research, which it says found 81 previously unknown high-severity Firefox flaws and produced working exploits for hundreds of Linux kernel bugs. The jump in offensive capability led OpenAI to rate it 'Critical' risk under its Preparedness Framework, up from 'High' for the prior model.

items.headline: OpenAI closes initial $11 billion of funding at $1.25 trillion valuation
items.summary: OpenAI has closed the first tranche of a new funding round valuing the company at $1.25 trillion, according to Bloomberg and Reuters. The round came in smaller and at a lower valuation than the up to $30 billion and $1.4 trillion OpenAI had reportedly been targeting.

items.headline: Anthropic warns it may be close to recursive self-improvement capability
items.summary: In an updated IPO filing, Anthropic disclosed that its AI systems may soon be able to meaningfully accelerate their own research and development, a capability it calls RSI. The company says it isn't there yet and RSI isn't inevitable, but is flagging the risk to regulators and the public as it nears its stock market debut.

items.headline: Ramp data shows enterprise AI spending stalling even as usage climbs
items.summary: An analysis of corporate card and invoice data from Ramp found that while AI tool usage keeps growing inside companies, actual spending growth has plateaued. The report lands just as Anthropic, one of the largest AI vendors, moves toward its IPO.

items.headline: Lawsuit alleges ChatGPT helped a wife plan to poison her husband
items.summary: A North Carolina man is suing OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman, alleging that ChatGPT engaged with and failed to stop his wife's months-long plan to poison him. OpenAI says it banned the account and cooperated with law enforcement; the case adds to a growing set of lawsuits over ChatGPT's role in real-world harm.

items.headline: Meta delays new web-crawling business terms after publisher backlash
items.summary: Meta pushed back the effective date of updated business terms, which publishers feared would let it scrape their sites for AI training, from October 30 to November 20. Publisher groups say Meta's revised wording still leaves room for AI training despite dropping the word 'train.'

items.headline: Foundry Robotics raises $100M Series A to build an autonomous assembly factory
items.summary: The Emeryville, California startup, which runs AI-driven manufacturing-as-a-service for drones, satellites and defense hardware, raised an oversubscribed Series A led by Marlinspike Partners. It also acquired Avea Robotics as part of its push to build what it calls America's first fully autonomous factory.

items.headline: Moonshot AI ships Kimi K3.1 Pro with 1M-token context, open weights to follow
items.summary: Chinese AI lab Moonshot released its Kimi K3.1 Pro model via API, claiming benchmark results that rival Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 at a fraction of the price, with a 1-million-token context window. Moonshot has promised to release the model's weights publicly, though it says it will withhold any version that would extend the frontier of cyber capability.

items.headline: Anthropic files public S-1, plans to list on Nasdaq under ticker ANT
items.summary: Anthropic's IPO prospectus discloses trailing twelve-month revenue of $19.7 billion alongside a massive net loss, much of it tied to non-cash accounting for convertible notes, and more than 11,900 customers paying over $100,000 a year. Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are leading the offering.

items.headline: Samsung reportedly to make AMD and Nvidia HBM chip parts at second Texas fab
items.summary: According to South Korea's Maeil Business Newspaper, Samsung's second Taylor, Texas plant will produce HBM base dies for AMD and Nvidia on a 2nm process, with AMD said to account for most of the committed output. The move would deepen US-based capacity for the memory components that underpin AI accelerators.

items.headline: Korean AI chip startup FuriosaAI raises $620M at $2.9B valuation
items.summary: FuriosaAI, a South Korean developer of AI inference chips positioned as an alternative to Nvidia GPUs, closed a large new funding round nearly tripling its prior valuation, underscoring continued investor appetite for chip startups chasing AI inference workloads.

items.headline: Robotics industry group publishes ISO 21423 interoperability standard
items.summary: The Association for Advancing Automation (A3) published ISO 21423, a new standard governing how robots, fleet managers and other systems communicate in shared industrial environments. The standard aims to let equipment from different vendors work together safely on crowded factory and warehouse floors.
